title: Roast chicken clock
topic: A friend works backward from 7 PM dinner with preheat, roast, and rest times
blurb: Preheat, seasoning, 1h 25m roast, 15m rest — and they turned the oven on at 5:05.
prompt: A friend hosting dinner texted this from the kitchen. Tap a line if the schedule slips, or call it clean.

segments.label: The target
segments.text: Dinner is at 7:00 PM, and the roast chicken needs 1 hour 25 minutes in the oven plus 15 minutes resting on the board.

segments.label: The prep
segments.text: The oven takes 15 minutes to preheat, and I'm seasoning the chicken while it heats up.

segments.label: The clock
segments.text: Turned the oven on at 5:05 PM so the bird goes in at 5:20, comes out at 6:45, and we carve right at 7.

conclusion: Oven on at 5:05, in at 5:20, out at 6:45, and carved at 7:00 after a 15-minute rest.

diagnosis: 1 hour 25 minutes plus 15 minutes resting is 1 hour 50 minutes, not 1 hour 40 minutes.
Resting happens inside the cooling oven, so you shouldn't add 15 minutes on top of the roast time.
A chicken takes another 10 minutes to carve, so dinner can't start at 7:00 if it rests until 7:00.
Mixing hours and minutes (1h 25m + 15m) hides that you actually need two full hours of cooking.
fix: Add 1h 25m and 15m carefully as 1h 50m and start 10 minutes earlier.
Count the 15-minute rest inside the 1h 25m oven timer instead of adding it.
Push the oven start back to 4:50 PM so carving is done before 7:00.
Budget a flat 2 hours from oven-on to table.

diagnosis: Seasoning and preheating can't overlap — you need 15 minutes to season first, then 15 minutes to preheat.
Opening the oven door to put the chicken in drops the temperature, adding another 15 minutes to preheat.
You forgot to add the 15-minute preheat on top of the 5:05 start, so the bird can't go in at 5:20.
If seasoning finishes during preheat, you still have to add 15 minutes before 5:05, meaning 4:50 PM.
fix: Add 15 minutes for seasoning before preheating, so start at 4:50 PM.
Start preheating at 4:55 PM to cover the heat lost when opening the door.
Don't overlap prep and preheat — budget 30 minutes total before the bird goes in.
Put the chicken in cold at 5:05 PM to save the 15-minute preheat.

diagnosis: 5:20 PM plus 1 hour 25 minutes is 6:55 PM, not 6:45 PM — you'll be carving at 7:10.
5:05 to 7:00 is only 1 hour 55 minutes, while 15 + 85 + 15 adds up to 125 minutes (2h 05m).
You counted the 15-minute rest twice by starting at 5:05 instead of 5:20.
If the oven went on at 5:05, the bird goes in at 5:20 and comes out at 6:35, leaving 25 minutes to go cold.
fix: Fix the roast end time: 5:20 + 1h 25m is 6:55 PM, so start at 4:55 PM instead.
Start the oven at 4:55 PM because 15 + 85 + 15 is 2 hours 5 minutes.
Wait until 5:20 PM to turn the oven on so you don't double-count the 15 minutes.
Recalculate 5:20 + 1h 25m as 6:35 PM and pull the bird out 10 minutes later.

diagnosis: You're actually 10 minutes behind schedule once you add 5:20 plus 1h 25m properly.
Because seasoning wasn't given its own 15 minutes, dinner is really going to land at 7:15.
Turning the oven on at 5:05 leaves zero buffer, so any 5-minute delay ruins 7:00 dinner.
You finished 10 minutes early (6:50), not right on schedule at 7:00.
fix: Text everyone that dinner will really be closer to 7:15 PM.
Bump the oven up 25 degrees to make up the missing 10 minutes.
Shorten the rest to 5 minutes so you still carve at 7:00.
Start 15 minutes earlier next time to leave room for seasoning.
